makaleler.baslik_en: Subsidies and Behavioral Interventions to Increase Online Fruit and Vegetable Purchasing: A Pilot Randomized Clinical Trial.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Subsidies and Behavioral Interventions to Increase Online Fruit and Vegetable Purchasing: A Pilot Randomized Clinical Trial.
makaleler.ozet_en: IMPORTANCE: The US population eats less than the recommended amounts of fruits and vegetables despite known health benefits. Innovative solutions to increase fruits and vegetables purchasing are needed. OBJECTIVE: To examine whether fruits and vegetables subsidies, choice architecture, and/or loss-framed text message reminders increase fruits and vegetables purchases in an online shopping store.

makaleler.baslik_en: Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair for Severe Isolated Tricuspid Regurgitation After Extended Follow-Up: The TRI-FR Randomized Clinical Trial.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair for Severe Isolated Tricuspid Regurgitation After Extended Follow-Up: The TRI-FR Randomized Clinical Trial.
makaleler.ozet_en: BACKGROUND: Transcatheter tricuspid edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER) improves symptoms and health status at 1 year in patients with severe tricuspid regurgitation, but its association with clinical events during longer follow-up remains uncertain. METHODS: This secondary analysis reports extended follow-up of TRI-FR (URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04646811), a prospectively registered, multicenter randomized trial comparing T-TEER plus optimized medical therapy (OMT) with OMT alone in patients with severe symptomatic tricuspid regurgitation. In total, 300 patients were randomized (152 to T-TEER plus OMT and 148 to OMT alone).

makaleler.baslik_en: Autoantibody origins in lupus and upon recurrence post CAR-T therapy.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Autoantibody origins in lupus and upon recurrence post CAR-T therapy.
makaleler.ozet_en: Anti-CD19 chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T therapy induces profound remissions in lupus by depleting B cells, challenging the view that disease is sustained by long-lived plasma cells. Using molecular antibody tagging in mouse models of monogenic childhood-onset lupus, we show that autoantibody-producing plasma cells are short-lived and require continuous replenishment from T-bet-dependent precursors derived from long-lived B cell cohorts. The spleen is a major plasma cell reservoir, with perivascular enrichment observed in patients with lupus. Both anti-CD19 and anti-B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA) CAR-T therapies eliminate anti-DNA antibodies.
